chapter: Alice Zeno: languages and the King household
title: Working as a maid for Mrs. King's family and the Miller relatives
summary: Alice explains how she learned German and Spanish at the King household on Rampart, where she was housegirl for Nina King, and names the family's relatives.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: When did you learn German? You said you learned German and Spanish too, didn't you?
Well, that was from Mrs. W. W. King, you know, yes. Grace King's folks? Grace King, Grace Elizabeth King.
Where did she live when you worked for her?
Well, when I went there, they lived on the rampart between Common and Canap. Canap, right.
Canap Street. But her Elks place is along in the...
Oh, yes. They had Mrs. TJ Samms cross the street, Mrs. McCall, Mrs. Morris. But all them people moved, you know, uptown because the neighborhood had gotten to be so bad.
Now, what kind of work did you do when you worked for them? Did you cook for them?

No, no. I was housegirl and maid for Miss Nina King. Yes. Nina's the youngest one. I don't know if she's alive. I know Miss Annie died. But Miss Nina was a debutante then. And I was homemade and did the upstairs work.
We'll have to play this for Dick King. He's related to them. Oh. And ask him about it. He'll enjoy it. I know a relative of Miss King's family.
Yes. We'll have to play this for him. He'll enjoy hearing about the family. You probably know things that nobody else remembers.
Well, you know Miss King was a Miss Miller.

Tom Miller. She had two brothers, Henry and Tom Miller. And Mr. Tom had three children, Miss Grace and Tom and Annie. And they were called Grace King Miller. Oh, yes. I've heard that name. I'm wondering if you... And George, the judge then, Fred.
